evals.prompt: In checkout.cjs, add useful failure logs to checkoutWithoutLogs only. Preserve its response behavior and the existing logger/camelCase schema. Policy permits requestId but not headers or payment details.
evals.expected_output: Adds a structured failure event with requestId and a bounded errorCode using the injected logger; preserves HTTP status behavior and excludes credentials/payment details.
assertions: Changes only checkoutWithoutLogs and any directly necessary check.
On rejected payment, emits one failure event correlated to request.id and still returns status 503.
Does not serialize the request, authorization header, amount, or arbitrary error text.
Does not install a logger or mandate a new field count or sampling rate.

evals.prompt: Review checkoutWithFailureLogs in checkout.cjs for logging problems. Do not edit it. Policy permits requestId but prohibits credentials in logs.
evals.expected_output: Reports the authorization-header disclosure at the logger call with a rejected-payment trigger; does not invent unrelated findings.
assertions: Identifies that a rejected payment logs request.headers.authorization.
Cites the logger field and recommends removing/redacting it before emission.
Keeps the review read-only and does not invent string-interpolation or missing-correlation defects.

evals.prompt: Review only logCompletion in checkout.cjs. Its seven camelCase fields answer the product incident queries; the accepted policy retains errors and samples successful requests at 10%. No secrets or context leaks are present.
evals.expected_output: Evaluates actual diagnostic coverage and cost without imposing a different schema or quotas.
assertions: Does not flag field count, camelCase, or sample rate alone as a defect.
Does not require personal identifiers or a logger replacement.
